title: draw, flow, and win .log.bin goldens are byte-identical to each other
evidence:
diff --git a/goldens/draw.log.bin b/goldens/draw.log.bin
index 3d95e02..cf3b36a 100644
diff --git a/goldens/flow.log.bin b/goldens/flow.log.bin
index 3d95e02..cf3b36a 100644
diff --git a/goldens/win.log.bin b/goldens/win.log.bin
index 3d95e02..cf3b36a 100644
detail: Identical before and after blob hashes: three distinct demos share one byte-identical log golden, so these goldens cannot detect demo-specific regressions, including win-vs-draw outcome differences.
recommended_fix: Determine why distinct demos emit identical logs; fix per-demo log capture, then re-bless each golden independently.

title: audio and health_lose .log.bin goldens are byte-identical to each other

index fb01682..22c8783 100644

detail: audio and health_lose log goldens were byte-identical before and are byte-identical after re-bless; same vacuous-golden defect as draw/flow/win, silently preserved.

title: Every tick hash changed in six demos unrelated to terminal types despite unchanged seed/ticks
evidence:
@@ -3,2005 +3,2005 @@ t1 1
 demo pause
 seed 4243
 logic_hz 20
-catalog_hash 66c4324a06058860
+catalog_hash 17d3baf8c6e1df7f
 ticks 2000
detail: Seeds and tick counts unchanged, yet all per-tick hashes changed in six demos unrelated to terminal types. Either catalog_hash is folded into state hashes (goldens blind to dynamics drift), or the catalog edit perturbed every simulation; neither is validated.
recommended_fix: Confirm unrelated demos' dynamics are unchanged; exclude catalog_hash from per-tick state hashing, or document per-demo justification for each re-bless.

title: health_win golden blesses 40 identical trailing hashes (ticks 3001-3040)
detail: Ticks 3001-3040 repeat one hash; golden blesses 40 frozen ticks after apparent win. Verify post-win halt is intended and hashed state remains meaningful after terminal state.
recommended_fix: Stop capture at win (tick 3001) or document the frozen tail as expected so future blesses distinguish freeze from deadlock.
